text: The map forgets only the proof Wp(μ₀,μ)<∞. Two subtype elements with the same probability law are therefore equal by proof irrelevance. This matches the [actual anchored subtype](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L77); it is not a quotient of laws by zero transport distance. The published [reconstruction identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L157) checks that forgetting and restoring membership preserves the element. The assertion needs no finite moment of μ₀ or point separation.
Published reconstruction from the underlying law and stored finite-anchor-distance proof.

The hypothesis is equality of the underlying probability measures, so subtype extensionality gives equality of the component elements. This is exactly the advertised equality principle for [the anchored subtype](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L77). It does not infer equality from zero distance on a pseudometric base. The [published injection theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L115) supplies the same implication without exposing proof fields. Different proofs of finite anchor distance cannot create distinct elements.
Actual equality of underlying probability laws determines the component element.

This instance supplies measurable ground edist and p≥1 to the [actual distance constructor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L169). Borel compatibility and second countability justify measurability; standard-Borel structure supports gluing in the triangle law. The [published evaluation Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L193) confirms the installed distance is Wp of the underlying laws. It therefore realizes the component pseudometric specified by [Layer 3.2](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L510), including p=∞, without asserting separation or identifying an arbitrary anchor’s component with Pp.
Evaluation of the canonical component edist as Wp.
Published pseudometric Dirac regression; zero-distance atoms have equal Borel Dirac laws and zero Wasserstein distance.

The left side uses the canonical component instance, whose defining distance is exactly Wp of the two underlying probability measures. Thus this is the precise evaluation equation promised by [the constructor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L169). There is no normalization by the anchor or subtraction of its distances. The published [pairwise finiteness theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L201) then bounds this same quantity through the common anchor. The equation includes p=∞ under the instance’s p≥1 assumptions.
Finite distance between laws in the same anchored component via the common anchor.

Finite-moment laws form a subtype of probability measures. Forgetting the moment proof therefore preserves and reflects equality of elements, as [the carrier definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L88) requires. This agrees with [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s Pp being a subset of probability laws. The [published reconstruction identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L308) checks the projection loses no law data. The result is independent of any basepoint witness, moment proof, or metric separation theorem.
Reconstruction returns exactly the original finite-moment law.

Equality of the underlying probability laws gives equality in the finite-moment subtype; the two proofs of finite moment are irrelevant. This is the equality relation of [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s Pp, implemented by [the published injectivity theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L269). The premise is literal law equality, not equality of densities at every point or equality of selected moment witnesses. No completeness, positive exponent or metric-separation hypothesis is needed for this carrier-level fact.
Forgetting membership does not identify different laws.

The instance is exactly `Subtype.instMeasurableSpace`, pulled back from [Mathlib’s Giry measurable structure on probability measures](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/ProbabilityMeasure.lean#L265). It therefore follows the explicit [Layer 3.2 instruction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L510). The published [measurable inclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L285) and [measurable family constructor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L295) verify both directions of its subtype behavior. This construction needs no proof that the finite-moment subset is measurable. Equality with the Borel structure of the Wasserstein metric is a separate theorem, especially at p=∞.
The actual subtype inclusion is measurable in the inherited Giry structures.
A measurable law family with pointwise membership lifts measurably to the subtype.

The inclusion is measurable because the domain carries exactly the comap measurable structure along that inclusion. This is the standard subtype construction used by [Mathlib’s probability measures](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/ProbabilityMeasure.lean#L265) and explicitly required by [Layer 3.2](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L510). No assertion that the moment predicate defines a measurable ambient subset is needed. The theorem concerns the inherited Giry structures, so it makes no unsupported claim about the W∞ Borel topology.

A measurable probability-law family f whose every value has finite moment lifts measurably to the induced subtype. The underlying function remains f, as the [published constructor equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L290) checks. This is exactly the universal property of the inherited [Giry subtype structure](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/ProbabilityMeasure.lean#L265). The moment proofs need no separate measurability condition because they are propositions. The statement does not say that a merely measurable family becomes continuous in Wasserstein distance.
Construction preserves the supplied probability law exactly.

Forgetting an element’s finite-moment proof and reconstructing it with its own stored property returns exactly that element. This is the reverse constructor identity for [the actual subtype constructor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L257). Together with [the forward projection equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L290), it checks that the carrier contains the original probability law rather than a normalized or selected replacement. Equality is independent of which proof certifies its moment condition.
Construction preserves the supplied probability law exactly.

The Dirac-component identification leaves μ’s underlying probability measure unchanged; only its membership proof changes from finite moment to finite distance from δx₀. The equality is exactly what [the definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L319) promises. The [published inverse equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L337) checks the same fact in the other direction. The Dirac anchor has finite moment, so this carrier comparison is justified without asserting the analogous claim for an arbitrary anchor.
The inverse Dirac-component map preserves the underlying probability law.

Both laws carry finite p-moment proofs. The product coupling then has finite Lp displacement by the [published moment-transfer theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L754), so its cost bounds Wp by a finite value. This is [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s finiteness argument for Pp. The ordinary pseudometric and measurable-distance assumptions are explicit, and the proof works at p=∞ with bounded distance sections. It does not identify an unrestricted arbitrary-anchor component with Pp or require the missing Cauchy specialization.
Published fixed-plan moment comparison gives finite displacement for the product coupling of two finite-moment laws.

Nonnegative weights a+b=1 make the displayed sum a probability measure. The published [moment scaling](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L448) and [moment addition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L722) results keep it in Pp, yielding exactly the requested law ρ. This is closure of [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s finite-moment carrier under ordinary mixtures. The equality fixes ρ’s underlying measure, so the existential does not select a different law. Zero weights and p=∞ are valid; the statement asserts mixture convexity, not geodesic convexity.
Finite scalar multiplication preserves the actual moment predicate.
Addition of finite measures with finite moment preserves that predicate, including∞.

Each pairwise Wp is finite, each NNReal weight is finite, and a finite sum of their nonnegative powers remains finite. This proves precisely the displayed expression. For 1≤p<∞ it is the usual weighted p-cost; the published [Fréchet consumer](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/FrechetMean.lean#L43) explicitly imposes that range. At p=∞, `p.toReal=0`, so this helper merely bounds the resulting sum of weights; it does not define the endpoint barycenter objective. Empty index sets and zero weights remain valid.
Pairwise Wasserstein values on Pp are genuinely finite before taking toReal.

The instance passes the Borel-measurable ground distance and p≥1 to the [published Wp constructor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L442). Standard-Borel structure supports its triangle law, while the [evaluation Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L465) confirms the installed edist is the actual Wasserstein value. This is [Layer 3.2’s pseudometric construction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L510). It includes p=∞ without importing finite-p topology or density claims. A pseudometric is correctly asserted before any separate proof of separation.
Evaluation of the canonical finite-moment edist as Wp.
Published pseudometric Dirac regression; zero-distance atoms have equal Borel Dirac laws and zero Wasserstein distance.

The canonical instance defines extended distance by Wp of the underlying probability laws. This equation therefore connects metric notation to exactly the transport quantity in [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s Pp construction, including the separately supported infinity endpoint. It introduces no normalization or replacement of measures. The [published pairwise-finiteness theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L405) applies to this same value and justifies the later conversion to a real pseudometric.
Pairwise Wasserstein values on Pp are genuinely finite before taking toReal.

The real distance is the real value of Wp, exactly as claimed. The crucial supporting fact is [published finiteness for both finite-moment laws](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L405): `ENNReal.toReal` is never being applied to an infinite distance here. The formula thus realizes the ordinary finite distance of [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s Pp space. It covers p=∞ under the installed p≥1 pseudometric assumptions without asserting that the endpoint has the finite-p topology.
Pairwise Wasserstein values on Pp are genuinely finite before taking toReal.

Both edists are Wp of the underlying laws, and the [published coercion identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L331) shows that the Dirac-component map changes neither law. Their equality is therefore exact, with no rescaling or inequality loss. This is the distance compatibility required by [Layer 3.2](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L510). The statement fixes a Dirac anchor, includes p=∞ through the actual instances, and does not make an arbitrary-anchor identification.
The forward Dirac-component identification preserves the underlying law.

`Isometry` means preservation of every pairwise extended distance. That is exactly the [published distance equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L492) for the carrier equivalence with the Dirac-anchored component. Thus the statement gives an actual isometry, not merely a continuous or Lipschitz map. The [real-distance Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L509) also passes. The basepoint is explicit, both laws are unchanged, and p≥1 supports the metric structures including the infinity endpoint.
The Dirac-component identification preserves the real distance as well as edist.

The definition bundles the actual bijection `equivComponent x₀` with its proved isometry. Its inverse returns the same probability law with the converse finite-moment proof, as the [published inverse equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L337) checks. The [real-distance identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Space.lean#L509) confirms metric preservation. This realizes [Layer 3.2’s Dirac-component identification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport/README.md#L510) without choosing a new measure or invoking the unrestricted arbitrary-anchor claim. Pseudometric bases and p=∞ remain within the stated assumptions.
The inverse Dirac-component map preserves the underlying probability law.
The Dirac-component identification preserves the real distance as well as edist.
